In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the puffer fish species analysed in the present work (L. lagocephaluss, L. scelerattus and S. pachygaster) were non‐toxic in all the organs analysed (gills, liver, skin and flesh).
the puffer fish species L. sceleratsus is a potential threat in the Spanish coast.
the mELISA is a very useful tool for screening of tetrodotoxic puffer fish samples, and that the LC‐HRMS method is the most reliable technique for the identification of tetrodonic species.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of LC‐MS, LC‐MS/HRMS and mElISA in the analysis of Lagocephalous sceleratus samples from the Spanish coast, provides a valuable tool for food safety monitoring and for future risk assessment and management.
L. scelerats is an extremely toxic pufferfish species, which should be avoided for human consumption.
the use of a screening immunoanalytical method, such as mELISA, is a valuable tool to identify toxic puffer fish samples and, therefore, to avoid intoxications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mELISA method can be used as a screening tool for TTX presence in puffer fish samples, providing complementary functional data.
TTXs were detected in L. sceleratusthe only toxic species among the samples analysed.
the Mediterranean Sea is not free from pufferfish toxicity, and therefore, it is necessary to implement surveillance and risk assessment programs for the protection of human health.
